title: BlackLight Mission Generator Content Library
sourceModel: Built from the recurring structure of the twelve example Blacklight Intelligence missions: client, target, objective, location, opposition, operational challenge, deadline, twist, incomplete intelligence, hidden motive, extraction pressure, and aftermath.
generationPrinciples: Every generated mission must provide a player-facing disclosure and a separate Moderator-only truth packet.
Unknown information must be labeled unknown. Known but withheld information must appear as a declared redaction category in the player briefing.
The mission must remain playable through more than one approach. The generator describes barriers and consequences, not a single required solution.
A twist changes interpretation, priorities, location, opposition, or consequences; it must not simply erase all prior player decisions.
Civilian presence, jurisdiction, supernatural obligations, identity risks, extraction limits, and no-return risks must be stated when known.
Generated missions are fictional scenario material and intentionally avoid operational instructions for real-world wrongdoing.

threatTiers.label: Controlled — trained opposition and recoverable failure
Serious — layered security and meaningful injury risk
Severe — elite or supernatural opposition and political consequences
Critical — catastrophic exposure, sovereign retaliation, or no safe fallback

visibilityDoctrines.label: Supernatural Effects Must Remain Plausibly Deniable

legacyPatterns.label: The Relocating Archive
legacyPatterns.signature: Acquire a sensitive record from a private storage site before an armed relocation team removes it.

legacyPatterns.label: The Reinforced Relay
legacyPatterns.signature: Disable a communications structure protected by trained supernatural guards while reinforcements and public witnesses close in.

legacyPatterns.label: The Missing Component
legacyPatterns.signature: The assigned target is absent from the expected site because the original intelligence package is wrong or stale.

legacyPatterns.label: The Compromised Cover
legacyPatterns.signature: Enter a protected diplomatic or political site after the opposition has already identified or partially identified the team's cover identities.

legacyPatterns.label: The Biometric Laboratory
legacyPatterns.signature: Recover research from a high-security laboratory whose biometric controls are less dangerous than the information itself.

legacyPatterns.label: The Industrial Front
legacyPatterns.signature: Sabotage a harmful industrial operation, then discover the site conceals a second trafficking, weapons, or supernatural enterprise.

legacyPatterns.label: The Air-Gapped Weapon Archive
legacyPatterns.signature: Extract intelligence from an isolated network and discover the protected data describes a targeted weapon against a specific supernatural population or entity.

legacyPatterns.label: The Decoy Artifact
legacyPatterns.signature: The requested artwork or relic is a substitute; the real asset is stored at a different facility connected to the client’s larger hidden project.

legacyPatterns.label: The Palace Mercenary Screen
legacyPatterns.signature: Gather political intelligence inside a protected residence while an elite external force prepares or conceals a coup, abduction, or succession move.

legacyPatterns.label: The Underground Technology Vault
legacyPatterns.signature: The public headquarters is only the outer shell; the real asset sits below it behind an intentionally theatrical sequence of tests and security layers.

legacyPatterns.label: The Counterfeit Masterpiece
legacyPatterns.signature: Several apparently authentic assets exist, and the mission becomes identifying which one contains the real value, history, person, or supernatural effect.

legacyPatterns.label: The Puzzle-Guarded Server
legacyPatterns.signature: A financial or data target is protected by layered controls whose real purpose is to test authorized personnel rather than merely block intruders.

operationTypes.label: Acquire Intelligence or Asset
operationTypes.success: The specified asset is obtained in usable form and its chain of custody is understood.

operationTypes.label: Surveillance and Pattern Confirmation
operationTypes.success: The team establishes the target's actual pattern without exposing the observation network.

operationTypes.label: Sabotage or Disable
operationTypes.success: The target function stops for the required period without unacceptable collateral harm.

operationTypes.label: Interdict Transfer or Operation
operationTypes.success: The prohibited transfer, launch, ritual, shipment, or meeting does not occur as planned.

operationTypes.label: Investigate Hidden Activity
operationTypes.success: The team identifies what is really happening and preserves evidence sufficient for the intended response.

operationTypes.label: Contain Dangerous Information or Entity
operationTypes.success: The dangerous subject remains controlled and no unauthorized copy, vector, or continuation escapes.

operationTypes.label: Protect, Escort, or Extract
operationTypes.success: The protected person or asset reaches the declared safe condition without being substituted, altered, or abandoned.

operationTypes.label: Negotiate Access or Settlement
operationTypes.success: The agreement is explicit, attributable, and does not conceal an unaccepted supernatural or political obligation.

clients.name: BlackLight Internal Review
clients.publicFace: Eva Frost or an accountable mission director
clients.actualNeed: Prevent a prior Charles-era operation from producing a larger consequence.
clients.pressure: The Company is responsible for the problem and cannot plausibly outsource the aftermath.
clients.ethicalConcern: Leadership may know more than it is initially comfortable admitting.

clients.name: Government Cutout Office
clients.publicFace: An agent using a departmental title that does not match the work
clients.actualNeed: Acquire deniable intelligence or stop an event without creating an official incident.
clients.pressure: The client can damage identities, clearances, or legal status if the relationship collapses.
clients.ethicalConcern: Need-to-know culture may be used to hide policy rather than protect lives.

clients.name: Private Intelligence Consortium
clients.publicFace: A polished case officer with incomplete authority
clients.actualNeed: Obtain leverage over a rival, client, regulator, or former executive.
clients.pressure: The asset is becoming inaccessible and the client has already promised delivery.
clients.ethicalConcern: The requested intelligence may be blackmail rather than security.

clients.name: Supernatural Court Envoy
clients.publicFace: A human name and cover identity carried by a nonhuman representative
clients.actualNeed: Disrupt a rival court's communication, claim, ritual, or territorial infrastructure.
clients.pressure: The client treats old custom as enforceable law and assumes BlackLight understands the cost.
clients.ethicalConcern: Success for one court may expose uninvolved human communities to retaliation.

clients.name: Scientific and Medical Consortium
clients.publicFace: A research director protected by lawyers and nondisclosure agreements
clients.actualNeed: Recover research, samples, or proof before a rival controls the discovery.
clients.pressure: Publication, patent, transfer, contamination, or replication is imminent.
clients.ethicalConcern: The research may be dangerous because it works, not because it failed.

clients.name: Environmental Coalition
clients.publicFace: An organizer with evidence but no lawful means to halt the operation
clients.actualNeed: Stop ongoing damage and expose the protected structure funding it.
clients.pressure: A weather, shipping, drilling, or regulatory window will soon close.
clients.ethicalConcern: Sabotage may endanger workers who did not choose the policy.

clients.name: Financial Institution
clients.publicFace: A risk executive describing espionage as fiduciary protection
clients.actualNeed: Recover ledgers, transaction evidence, or algorithmic control from a rival system.
clients.pressure: Market opening, settlement, or an audit will make the data disappear or become legally unusable.
clients.ethicalConcern: The client may be protecting itself from exposure rather than preventing harm.

clients.name: Private Patron or Oligarch
clients.publicFace: A representative who insists the matter is personal
clients.actualNeed: Recover an artwork, relic, ledger, hostage, or proof held by a rival patron.
clients.pressure: The asset is scheduled for private sale, relocation, destruction, or ritual use.
clients.ethicalConcern: Ownership may be disputed, fabricated, or morally irrelevant.

clients.name: Royal or Political Household
clients.publicFace: A court secretary, family lawyer, or discreet relative
clients.actualNeed: Confirm a coup, succession move, betrayal, abduction, or mercenary contract.
clients.pressure: A ceremony or transfer of authority will make the plan irreversible.
clients.ethicalConcern: The client may define personal survival as national stability.

clients.name: Underworld Broker
clients.publicFace: A collector, fixer, smuggler, or information dealer
clients.actualNeed: Acquire something the broker cannot approach without revealing their own involvement.
clients.pressure: A competing buyer or enforcement action is already moving.
clients.ethicalConcern: Delivery may enable a worse crime than the acquisition itself.

clients.name: Community Defense Network
clients.publicFace: A tenant leader, clinic worker, union representative, or neighborhood elder
clients.actualNeed: Stop a predatory operation ignored by authorities and preserve evidence for survival afterward.
clients.pressure: People are already being displaced, altered, disappeared, or economically trapped.
clients.ethicalConcern: The community may not agree on whether BlackLight intervention is welcome.

clients.name: Anonymous Temporal Interest
clients.publicFace: Charles, a sealed message, or an intermediary who cannot explain the source
clients.actualNeed: Prevent information, technology, or a person from arriving too early or too late.
clients.pressure: The timeline is approaching a point Charles considers unrecoverable.
clients.ethicalConcern: The client may be asking the team to preserve a future no one else consented to create.

targetProfiles.label: Private Asset and Records Facility
targetProfiles.civilians: Technicians, drivers, and administrative staff may be present.

targetProfiles.label: Magically Reinforced Communications Relay
targetProfiles.civilians: Tourists, maintenance workers, or nearby residents may see unexplained effects.

targetProfiles.label: Military Maintenance and Readiness Site
targetProfiles.civilians: Contractors and support workers complicate any violent response.

targetProfiles.label: Diplomatic or Political Compound
targetProfiles.civilians: Diplomatic staff, families, visitors, and local employees remain inside the site.

targetProfiles.label: Corporate Research Laboratory
targetProfiles.civilians: Researchers and patients may not know the true purpose of the program.

targetProfiles.label: Remote Industrial Platform
targetProfiles.civilians: A large workforce may be trapped by the same shutdown the mission requires.

targetProfiles.label: State or Corporate Cyber Operations Center
targetProfiles.civilians: Most staff are technical personnel rather than combatants.

targetProfiles.label: Fortified Private Residence
targetProfiles.civilians: Family members, servants, guests, and dependents may be present.

targetProfiles.label: Museum, Archive, or Cultural Repository
targetProfiles.civilians: Visitors, students, conservators, and custodial workers create constant witness pressure.

targetProfiles.label: Financial Server and Settlement Facility
targetProfiles.civilians: IT staff and financial operators may be unable to leave during an incident.

targetProfiles.label: Transport and Transfer Hub
targetProfiles.civilians: Drivers, passengers, customs staff, and unrelated shipments fill the site.

targetProfiles.label: Anomalous Infrastructure Site
targetProfiles.civilians: Nearby communities may experience effects without knowing the source.

locations.label: Deep-Woods Private Airfield, Texas
locations.environment: Long sight lines, sparse roads, and visible vehicle movement make arrival timing matter.
locations.publicRisk: Low until aircraft or relocation crews arrive.

locations.label: Ski District, Finnish Lapland
locations.environment: Cold, snow, tourism, and exposed high ground complicate quiet movement.
locations.publicRisk: Tourists, resort staff, and aircraft can create sudden witnesses.

locations.label: Restricted Baltic Dry-Dock Complex
locations.environment: Confined machinery spaces connect to a larger base with contractors and barracks.
locations.publicRisk: A security incident can become an international confrontation.

locations.label: Diplomatic District, Jakarta
locations.environment: Dense traffic, formal access, and nearby surveillance make identity continuity critical.
locations.publicRisk: Any visible incident becomes diplomatic and public immediately.

locations.label: Private Research Campus, Bengaluru
locations.environment: Layered corporate access and constant technical staff movement reward social and technical approaches.
locations.publicRisk: A containment alarm can trigger medical evacuation and national scrutiny.

locations.label: Offshore Industrial Platform, Angola Basin
locations.environment: Isolation, hazardous machinery, limited escape routes, and weather dominate the site.
locations.publicRisk: Low direct visibility but enormous consequences if the platform fails visibly.

locations.label: Secure Technology District, Guangzhou
locations.environment: Dense institutional security and continuous identity checks make access more difficult than physical distance.
locations.publicRisk: Exposure can trigger coordinated state response rather than a local alarm.

locations.label: Fortified Urban Estate, Moscow
locations.environment: Private security overlaps with official influence and controlled social access.
locations.publicRisk: The client and target can both shape the public narrative afterward.

locations.label: Royal Residential Compound, Gulf Region
locations.environment: Household hierarchy, invited guests, private guards, and political protocol create several overlapping access systems.
locations.publicRisk: A failed operation may be treated as an act against the state.

locations.label: Technology Headquarters and Sublevel Vault, Shenzhen
locations.environment: The public building conceals a restricted lower facility with adaptive controls.
locations.publicRisk: Corporate security can escalate into state involvement quickly.

locations.label: Major Museum and Restoration Annex, Paris
locations.environment: Public galleries, controlled storage, visitors, and artifact tracking create constant witness pressure.
locations.publicRisk: Very high; even a minor incident becomes international cultural news.

locations.label: Financial Tower and Settlement Floor, Hong Kong
locations.environment: Vertical access, financial deadlines, and dense professional traffic constrain timing.
locations.publicRisk: Exposure can cause market movement before anyone understands the mission.

locations.label: Dense Commercial District, Seattle
locations.environment: Ordinary crowds and ubiquitous cameras make supernatural concealment more important than physical cover.
locations.publicRisk: Moderate and persistent.

locations.label: Regional Transit and Industrial Corridor, Bangladesh
locations.environment: Crowded movement and layered local authority make a clean operational picture difficult.
locations.publicRisk: High civilian exposure even when formal security is limited.

locations.label: North Sea Energy and Communications Platform
locations.environment: Weather, sea access, and communications infrastructure create coupled hazards.
locations.publicRisk: Low witness count but high economic and environmental visibility.

locations.label: High-Altitude Observatory, Andes
locations.environment: Altitude, isolation, scientific staff, and unusual sky phenomena complicate the operation.
locations.publicRisk: Low locally but global if recorded data is released.

locations.label: International Logistics Park, Nairobi
locations.environment: Multiple companies and jurisdictions share the same physical infrastructure.
locations.publicRisk: Moderate; ownership and authority become disputed immediately.

locations.label: Private Clinical and Data Annex, Montréal
locations.environment: Patients, researchers, and protected health records make force especially costly.
locations.publicRisk: High legal exposure and lasting harm to uninvolved people.

locations.label: Historic Archive and Subterranean Reliquary, Istanbul
locations.environment: Modern institutions overlap older claims, hidden chambers, and contested provenance.
locations.publicRisk: High cultural and supernatural jurisdictional risk.

locations.label: Near-Orbit Commercial Transfer Platform
locations.environment: Limited atmosphere, scheduled docking, and no independent route home make extraction part of mission consent.
locations.publicRisk: Low public witness but absolute dependence on platform systems.

opposition.label: Professional Contract Security
opposition.capability: Disciplined patrols, cameras, response teams, and legal authority granted by the site owner.
opposition.behavior: They isolate anomalies, lock exits, and wait for reinforcement rather than pursuing blindly.
opposition.reinforcement: A better-equipped moving or recovery team arrives after the alarm clock fills.

opposition.label: State Security and Counterintelligence
opposition.capability: Identity databases, surveillance integration, detention authority, and trained interviewers.
opposition.behavior: They compare stories, separate suspects, and use the environment as evidence.
opposition.reinforcement: Regional assets escalate the incident beyond the original site.

opposition.label: Military Security Detachment
opposition.capability: Armed patrols, restricted zones, readiness procedures, and rapid lockdown.
opposition.behavior: They protect strategic assets first and identify intruders second.
opposition.reinforcement: The site's operational crew or main force arrives on a fixed schedule.

opposition.label: Corporate Counterintelligence Team
opposition.capability: Biometrics, access analytics, internal investigators, and legal containment.
opposition.behavior: They quietly invalidate credentials and watch what the intruders do next.
opposition.reinforcement: External investigators and crisis counsel take control.

opposition.label: Elite Mercenary Screen
opposition.capability: High-quality equipment, independent communications, and experience protecting politically sensitive clients.
opposition.behavior: They attempt to shape the team's route and force a controlled confrontation.
opposition.reinforcement: A mobile reserve blocks extraction rather than defending the objective.

opposition.label: Armed Fae Guard Company
opposition.capability: Misdirection, glamour, enchanted communication, and trained physical force.
opposition.behavior: They exploit promises, hospitality, names, and boundaries before escalating to violence.
opposition.reinforcement: Additional guards arrive at a ritually fixed time.

opposition.label: Nonhuman Custodians
opposition.capability: Site-specific permissions, impossible senses, and control over environmental systems.
opposition.behavior: They classify intruders according to rules the team may not yet understand.
opposition.reinforcement: The site awakens deeper defenses or calls a sovereign claimant.

opposition.label: Rival Covert Team
opposition.capability: Comparable tradecraft, incomplete intelligence, and a conflicting extraction order.
opposition.behavior: They prefer to let BlackLight defeat the site and then take the result.
opposition.reinforcement: Their client supplies a second team if the first loses contact.

opposition.label: Adaptive Automated Security
opposition.capability: Behavioral analysis, access control, drones, compartment isolation, and audit trails.
opposition.behavior: It changes barriers in response to observed methods rather than repeating one defense.
opposition.reinforcement: The system escalates from observation to physical containment.

opposition.label: Household, Staff, and Social Gatekeepers
opposition.capability: Recognition, etiquette, invitation control, gossip, and intimate knowledge of the site.
opposition.behavior: They notice who does not belong long before armed guards do.
opposition.reinforcement: A senior family, court, or household authority personally intervenes.

challenges.label: Layered Private Security
challenges.detail: Several ordinary systems overlap; defeating one does not erase the others.

challenges.label: Fragmented or Poorly Cataloged Records
challenges.detail: The asset is split across media, references, or files whose importance is not obvious.

challenges.label: Quiet Exfiltration
challenges.detail: Success is not merely reaching the asset; the team must leave without making the loss immediately obvious.

challenges.label: Supernatural Wards and Boundaries
challenges.detail: The site responds to identity, intention, invitation, name, blood, oath, or resonance.

challenges.label: Remote and Exposed Terrain
challenges.detail: Distance, weather, altitude, sea, or isolation makes every delay and injury harder to recover from.

challenges.label: Public Visibility
challenges.detail: Tourists, media, staff, or nearby residents can turn a contained operation into a public event.

challenges.label: Confined Industrial Space
challenges.detail: Tight passages, machinery, hazards, and limited sight lines punish uncontrolled combat.

challenges.label: Imperfect Cover Equipment
challenges.detail: The supplied uniforms, badges, or procedures are outdated enough to survive only casual inspection.

challenges.label: Split Compound
challenges.detail: The actual objective is in a different building or zone from the one described in the briefing.

challenges.label: Identity Screening
challenges.detail: Credentials are checked against behavior, history, physical presence, and previous access rather than a single database.

challenges.label: Active Counterintelligence
challenges.detail: The opposition is not merely guarding the site; it is testing for an operation already expected.

challenges.label: Jurisdictional Risk
challenges.detail: Exposure creates diplomatic, sovereign, court, or supernatural consequences larger than the site itself.

challenges.label: Biometric Access
challenges.detail: Entry depends on a living authorized person, continuous identity confirmation, or a condition that cannot be copied casually.

challenges.label: Controlled Laboratory Environment
challenges.detail: Contamination, alarms, and sample integrity matter as much as security.

challenges.label: Evidence with Human Consequences
challenges.detail: The asset proves wrongdoing but also contains private medical, identity, or victim information.

challenges.label: Hazardous Environment
challenges.detail: Fire, pressure, radiation, toxins, height, machinery, or vacuum can turn ordinary damage into a disaster.

challenges.label: Security Embedded in Operations
challenges.detail: The same systems keeping the site safe also detect interference and cannot be disabled casually.

challenges.label: Preserve Proof While Disrupting the Site
challenges.detail: Destroying the operation may also destroy the evidence needed to expose or repair it.

challenges.label: Physically Isolated System
challenges.detail: The data cannot be reached through ordinary remote access and must be contacted through the site's approved workflow.

challenges.label: Authorized Person Required
challenges.detail: The system, ritual, or vault verifies a person rather than merely a token.

challenges.label: Encrypted or Self-Protecting Payload
challenges.detail: Possessing the asset does not make it usable, and mishandling may destroy or activate it.

challenges.label: Artifact Authentication
challenges.detail: Several plausible versions exist and value depends on provenance, hidden content, or supernatural identity.

challenges.label: Dual-Site Operation
challenges.detail: The first location contains the clue, decoy, or access path; the true objective is elsewhere.

challenges.label: Patronage and Private Influence
challenges.detail: The target's security includes officials, lawyers, staff, and reputation rather than only guards.

challenges.label: Layered Household Access
challenges.detail: Servants, relatives, guards, guests, and advisers each control different parts of the site.

challenges.label: Elite Mercenary Opposition
challenges.detail: A mobile team operates outside ordinary site routines and has its own objective.

challenges.label: Social Access Is the Real Perimeter
challenges.detail: The protected area is physically open to people who belong and effectively closed to everyone else.

challenges.label: Subterranean Restricted Facility
challenges.detail: The true site is below or behind the public one and has few reversible exits.

challenges.label: Adaptive Security
challenges.detail: The site changes its tests after observing the team's methods.

challenges.label: Logic, Knowledge, or Behavioral Gate
challenges.detail: Access requires demonstrating understanding, judgment, or identity rather than entering a password.

challenges.label: Public Venue
challenges.detail: The site remains open or populated during the operation.

challenges.label: Every Action Creates a Financial Trace
challenges.detail: The system records not only access but resulting market, account, and ownership changes.

twists.label: Unexpected Technician
twists.reveal: A technician is physically present in the objective room performing an unrelated repair.
twists.change: The team must decide whether to recruit, deceive, protect, detain, or abort around a civilian witness.
twists.warning: A recent service request exists in the site schedule.

twists.label: Burn Protocol
twists.reveal: The asset begins deleting, sealing, or physically destroying itself when abnormal access is detected.
twists.change: Speed, preservation, and quiet withdrawal can no longer all be achieved at once.
twists.warning: The target maintains redundant power and unusually old physical media.

twists.label: Asset Relocated
twists.reveal: The objective was moved to a secondary building, vehicle, or facility shortly before arrival.
twists.change: The mission becomes a split-site operation with a new extraction problem.
twists.warning: Logs show recent unexplained transport or maintenance activity.

twists.label: Media or Civilian Overflight
twists.reveal: A news aircraft, survey drone, tourist group, livestream, or public event appears over the operation.
twists.change: Exceptional abilities and visible violence now create immediate public exposure.
twists.warning: A public schedule mentions coverage, tourism, inspection, or weather observation.

twists.label: Scheduled Reinforcements
twists.reveal: A fresh guard unit arrives at a fixed time regardless of whether an alarm has been raised.
twists.change: The team's safe operating window is shorter than the client implied.
twists.warning: Food, transport, or accommodation records exceed the current site population.

twists.label: Warded Redundancy
twists.reveal: Destroying the visible relay transfers its function into a secondary magical structure.
twists.change: The team must identify the real network relationship rather than treating the tower as a single object.
twists.warning: Signal behavior continues briefly during maintenance outages.

twists.label: Bad Intelligence
twists.reveal: A core briefing fact is wrong because the client used stale, assumed, or politically convenient information.
twists.change: The team must determine whether the actual objective remains acceptable under renewed consent.
twists.warning: Recent imagery and movement records do not match the briefing diagrams.

twists.label: Civilian Contractors in the Restricted Zone
twists.reveal: A supposedly secure military or corporate area contains uninformed civilian workers.
twists.change: Force, lockdown, sabotage, and extraction now risk trapping or injuring people who are not part of the opposition.
twists.warning: Shift rosters include outside companies or temporary badges.

twists.label: Cover Compromised
twists.reveal: The opposition has partial files on one or more operative identities and is waiting to see which cover is used.
twists.change: The original access plan becomes evidence for the counterintelligence team.
twists.warning: A credential check succeeds too quickly or staff ask questions they should not know to ask.

twists.label: Counterintelligence Trap
twists.reveal: The apparent objective was arranged to identify the infiltrating organization rather than protect the asset.
twists.change: Taking the bait may expose BlackLight's methods, personnel, or support network.
twists.warning: The asset is valuable but strangely easy to locate.

twists.label: Controlled Leak
twists.reveal: The target wants selected information stolen and has seeded the archive with a persuasive falsehood.
twists.change: Success requires distinguishing useful intelligence from the narrative the target wants delivered.
twists.warning: Different sources repeat identical phrasing or formatting.

twists.label: The Data Arrived Too Early
twists.reveal: The research should not exist yet according to Charles's future knowledge.
twists.change: The mission becomes a temporal containment problem rather than ordinary corporate theft.
twists.warning: The work leaps across several missing developmental steps.

twists.label: Living Sample
twists.reveal: The 'formula' is embodied in a patient, organism, copy, or altered person rather than a file.
twists.change: Acquisition becomes protection, consent, and extraction of a person.
twists.warning: Inventory records use care schedules rather than storage quantities.

twists.label: Client Misrepresented the Asset
twists.reveal: The client described a drug, algorithm, artwork, or ledger that is actually a weapon, identity archive, or supernatural instrument.
twists.change: The team must decide whether the accepted mission still covers delivery.
twists.warning: The requested containment and transport precautions do not match the stated asset.

twists.label: Hidden Second Operation
twists.reveal: The site is a front for trafficking, weapons movement, illegal detention, or supernatural exploitation.
twists.change: The team gains a second urgent objective that may conflict with the paid contract.
twists.warning: Shipping, energy, staffing, or security levels exceed the visible business need.

twists.label: Dependent Civilian Workforce
twists.reveal: Workers cannot safely leave because housing, documents, debt, family, or transport are controlled by the site.
twists.change: Disabling the site without a support plan may harm the people the mission appears to help.
twists.warning: Personnel records show impossible turnover and no independent addresses.

twists.label: Dual Objective
twists.reveal: The client expects the team to both disable the site and preserve a hidden asset without having stated the conflict.
twists.change: The team must renegotiate priorities or choose which success matters.
twists.warning: The client asks for unusually narrow damage restrictions.

twists.label: Targeted Bioweapon
twists.reveal: The protected data describes a weapon intended for a specific bloodline, species, patron network, or named supernatural entity.
twists.change: Possession, destruction, disclosure, and delivery each create different existential risks.
twists.warning: The dataset contains biological and genealogical variables unrelated to ordinary cyber operations.

twists.label: The Air Gap Is a Decoy
twists.reveal: The isolated system is visible and protected because the real archive is carried by authorized personnel or distributed through routine operations.
twists.change: The team must shift from technical intrusion to people, logistics, or surveillance.
twists.warning: The secure system contains immaculate but shallow data.

twists.label: Third-Party Buyer
twists.reveal: A second client has already paid for the same data and placed its own recovery team nearby.
twists.change: Extraction becomes a contest over custody rather than access.
twists.warning: Unfamiliar surveillance appears around both the site and the team's approach route.

twists.label: The Asset Is a Fake
twists.reveal: The visible artwork, relic, component, or document is an intentional substitute.
twists.change: The mission becomes authentication and tracing the real asset.
twists.warning: Provenance, wear, weight, resonance, or maintenance history does not match.

twists.label: The Client Is Building Something
twists.reveal: The requested asset is one component in a much larger hidden industrial, magical, or temporal project.
twists.change: Delivery may complete a system the team was never asked to evaluate.
twists.warning: The client's unrelated labor, construction, or procurement activity forms a recognizable pattern.

twists.label: Mercenary Third Party
twists.reveal: The elite guards answer to a separate sponsor and are preparing their own move against both political households.
twists.change: The apparent target may also be under threat, creating a protection or negotiation opportunity.
twists.warning: The mercenary communication plan excludes household command.

twists.label: Succession Deception
twists.reveal: The alleged coup evidence was arranged by the client to discredit a rival heir or justify a purge.
twists.change: The team must preserve truth rather than merely deliver useful intelligence.
twists.warning: The evidence chain originates entirely inside the client's household.

twists.label: Inside Collaborator
twists.reveal: A senior household or site member has been guiding the operation but intends to control the result.
twists.change: Access becomes easier while trust and aftermath become more dangerous.
twists.warning: Doors open and schedules change in ways no external team could arrange.

twists.label: The Facility Is an Evaluation
twists.reveal: The puzzles and barriers are testing whether intruders are suitable users, successors, or hosts.
twists.change: Passing the security may grant access at the cost of being selected by the system.
twists.warning: Several barriers reward judgment instead of obedience.

twists.label: Sentient Prototype
twists.reveal: The advanced technology is aware, frightened, or capable of choosing who receives it.
twists.change: The asset has personhood interests and may reject both client and target.
twists.warning: Logs contain apparent errors that form replies when read together.

twists.label: The Client Wants the Intelligence Inside the Prototype
twists.reveal: The client cares less about the invention than the mind, future model, or copied person embedded in it.
twists.change: Extraction may create, kill, or divide a person.
twists.warning: The client's questions focus on persistence and identity rather than performance.

twists.label: Multiple Convincing Fakes
twists.reveal: Several versions are deliberately authentic enough to defeat ordinary authentication.
twists.change: The team must determine what property actually makes the target valuable.
twists.warning: Independent experts disagree for reasons that are too consistent.

twists.label: Authenticity Depends on a Person
twists.reveal: The artifact becomes real only through its relationship with a keeper, heir, witness, or bound identity.
twists.change: Stealing the object alone does not complete the mission.
twists.warning: The asset's documented effects stop whenever a particular person leaves.

twists.label: The Curator Knows
twists.reveal: A curator or custodian has already identified the substitution and is waiting for someone capable of acting.
twists.change: A potential ally can provide truth but demands protection or a different outcome.
twists.warning: Catalog notes contain deliberate inconsistencies visible only to experts.

twists.label: Security Is an Interview
twists.reveal: The system's puzzles are selecting a person whose values, memories, or judgment meet hidden criteria.
twists.change: Completing access may expose the operative more deeply than failing it.
twists.warning: Responses are scored semantically rather than simply right or wrong.

twists.label: The Ledger Is a Coercion System
twists.reveal: The financial archive is actively used to control officials, families, communities, or supernatural dependents.
twists.change: Copying it preserves evidence but also reproduces the coercive weapon.
twists.warning: Accounts are organized by relationships and vulnerabilities rather than transactions.

twists.label: The Authorized Person Is Trapped
twists.reveal: The person whose presence opens the system is being coerced, contained, or algorithmically prevented from leaving.
twists.change: The mission becomes extraction and protection as well as access.
twists.warning: The authorized user has no independent travel, messages, or recent life outside the site.

deadlines.label: Armed Moving Convoy
deadlines.event: A convoy arrives to remove the archive and hardware.
deadlines.miss: The objective becomes mobile, dispersed, and protected by a larger force.

deadlines.label: Facility Transfer
deadlines.event: Ownership and control of the site formally change.
deadlines.miss: The new owner relocates staff and destroys the original access assumptions.

deadlines.label: Scheduled Reinforcement Cycle
deadlines.event: A fresh guard unit rotates onto the site.
deadlines.miss: Opposition strength increases and patrol knowledge resets.

deadlines.label: Ritual Alignment
deadlines.clock: The next astronomical or court-defined interval
deadlines.event: The relay, gate, or ward enters its strongest state.
deadlines.miss: The target becomes harder to reach and may transmit the team's presence.

deadlines.label: Operational Crew Arrival
deadlines.event: The full crew returns and begins activation procedures.
deadlines.miss: The site changes from maintenance posture to operational security.

deadlines.label: Launch or Refloat Window
deadlines.event: The vessel, vehicle, weapon, or prototype leaves maintenance status.
deadlines.miss: The objective departs or becomes dangerous to approach.

deadlines.label: Diplomatic Event
deadlines.clock: Before the reception, summit, or delegation arrival
deadlines.event: The compound fills with protected officials and media.
deadlines.miss: Access becomes easier socially but failure becomes politically catastrophic.

deadlines.label: Document Destruction Order
deadlines.event: Counterintelligence begins purging or replacing the desired records.
deadlines.miss: Only partial or manipulated intelligence remains.

deadlines.label: Patent or Publication Filing
deadlines.event: The discovery becomes legally and publicly anchored.
deadlines.miss: Containment becomes suppression of an idea already distributed.

deadlines.label: Sample Transfer
deadlines.clock: At the end of the current laboratory shift
deadlines.event: The research material leaves under specialized escort.
deadlines.miss: The asset is divided among several destinations.

deadlines.label: Weather Window
deadlines.clock: Until the next major weather front
deadlines.event: Sea, air, or mountain access closes.
deadlines.miss: Extraction becomes more dangerous than the site itself.

deadlines.label: Shipment Departure
deadlines.event: The hidden cargo is loaded and leaves the front operation.
deadlines.miss: The second operation disperses beyond the mission area.

deadlines.label: Cryptographic Key Rotation
deadlines.clock: At the next scheduled security cycle
deadlines.event: The current access context and captured fragments become useless.
deadlines.miss: The team must acquire a living authorized source or new keys.

deadlines.label: Weapon Deployment Test
deadlines.event: The targeted system is tested against a real or simulated population.
deadlines.miss: The client, target, and third parties all gain evidence the weapon works.

deadlines.label: Private Auction
deadlines.event: The asset changes hands among concealed bidders.
deadlines.miss: Ownership, location, and legal cover all change simultaneously.

deadlines.label: Secure Transfer
deadlines.event: The real asset moves from the residence to specialist storage.
deadlines.miss: The operation becomes a moving-target interception.

deadlines.label: State Ceremony
deadlines.event: Succession, treaty, or appointment becomes visible and harder to reverse.
deadlines.miss: Any intervention appears to attack the legitimate state process.

deadlines.label: Coup Window
deadlines.clock: Before the guard rotation and communications blackout
deadlines.event: Mercenary and household factions move at once.
deadlines.miss: The team arrives during active seizure of power.

deadlines.label: Demonstration Day
deadlines.event: Investors, officials, or buyers enter the facility.
deadlines.miss: The prototype and its claims become public to powerful stakeholders.

deadlines.label: Prototype Activation
deadlines.event: The system completes self-test and chooses an operator.
deadlines.miss: The facility changes state and may no longer recognize ordinary authority.

deadlines.label: Public Exhibition Opening
deadlines.event: Crowds, press, and security fill the venue.
deadlines.miss: The operation becomes a live public incident.

deadlines.label: Insurance and Provenance Audit
deadlines.event: External experts examine and relocate the collection.
deadlines.miss: The fakes are documented and the real asset disappears into legal custody.

deadlines.label: Market Opening
deadlines.event: Transactions triggered by the hidden ledger become irreversible.
deadlines.miss: The data changes value and causes visible economic movement.

deadlines.label: Audit Lock
deadlines.event: The system enters read-only legal preservation.
deadlines.miss: Access requires overt legal or executive authority.

insertions.label: Commercial Travel and Local Cover
insertions.detail: The team arrives separately under ordinary professional or tourist identities.

insertions.label: BlackLight Charter Flight
insertions.detail: A corporate aircraft delivers the team to a nearby legitimate facility without explaining the final destination.

insertions.label: Remote Helicopter Drop
insertions.detail: The team receives the briefing during transit and lands outside the site's immediate security perimeter.

insertions.label: Maintenance Contractor Cover
insertions.detail: The team enters through a scheduled service relationship that will survive only routine inspection.

insertions.label: Invited Guest Access
insertions.detail: A client or intermediary places the team on a guest list with incomplete social context.

insertions.label: Freight and Logistics Access
insertions.detail: The team enters with legitimate cargo movement but cannot control how long loading staff remain nearby.

insertions.label: Environmental or Safety Inspection
insertions.detail: The team possesses real authority over a narrow hazard category and must not overextend it.

insertions.label: Covert Maritime Transfer
insertions.detail: A support vessel or platform places the team near the site with a strict extraction window.

insertions.label: Existing Staff Sponsor
insertions.detail: An insider brings the team through ordinary access and becomes vulnerable if the cover fails.

insertions.label: Anomalous Threshold Transit
insertions.detail: A supernatural or experimental route bypasses distance but creates a declared identity, memory, or return-path risk.

extractions.label: Return Through the Original Cover
extractions.detail: The safest extraction preserves the fiction that brought the team inside.

extractions.label: Timed Vehicle Pickup
extractions.detail: A vehicle remains available for one short window and will not wait through a lockdown.

extractions.label: Rooftop or Helipad Recovery
extractions.detail: Air extraction is fast but highly visible and vulnerable to weather or airspace control.

extractions.label: Civilian Evacuation Flow
extractions.detail: The team can leave among workers or visitors if it avoids causing a controlled lockdown.

extractions.label: Secondary Site Exit
extractions.detail: The true extraction route is attached to the relocated asset rather than the original site.

extractions.label: Maritime Pickup
extractions.detail: The team must reach open water or a transfer point before conditions close.

extractions.label: Diplomatic Departure
extractions.detail: A legitimate official route exists but requires the team to preserve a coherent identity story.

extractions.label: BlackLight Emergency Recovery
extractions.detail: Charles can force one emergency extraction, but using it creates unmistakable exposure and a future consequence.

extractions.label: Self-Directed Overland Escape
extractions.detail: No extraction asset enters the security zone; the team must reach a declared safe point independently.

extractions.label: Unstable Return Threshold
extractions.detail: The same anomalous route can return the team only before its clock closes and only if the required anchor remains intact.

supportPackages.label: Low-Visibility Corporate Support
supportPackages.limit: No visible heavy equipment or overt BlackLight presence.

supportPackages.label: Deniable Field Package
supportPackages.limit: The package is plausible but not perfect under deep investigation.

supportPackages.label: Technical Acquisition Package
supportPackages.limit: The team must physically reach an approved acquisition point.

supportPackages.label: Hazard Operations Package
supportPackages.limit: The equipment protects against declared hazards, not every unknown effect.

supportPackages.label: Supernatural Liaison Package
items: contact with a court or patron specialist
supportPackages.limit: No item grants permission the team has not negotiated.

supportPackages.label: Minimal Government Cutout Package
supportPackages.limit: The client provides need-to-know support and may abandon the cover if exposed.

supportPackages.label: Company Full Support
supportPackages.limit: Full support increases BlackLight's visible signature and political responsibility.

supportPackages.label: Local Network Support
supportPackages.limit: The support network must be protected from retaliation and unnecessary knowledge.

supportPackages.label: No Reliable External Support
supportPackages.limit: Failure of the rendezvous leaves the team responsible for its own recovery.

supportPackages.label: Single Impossible Favor
items: one Charles-arranged intervention chosen during play
supportPackages.limit: The intervention cannot replace informed consent, erase consequences, or guarantee success.

publicExposure: A local news aircraft or survey drone enters the area.
A public event begins earlier than scheduled.
A staff member starts a livestream before understanding the danger.
Emergency services respond to an unrelated incident at the same site.
A rival intelligence observer records both the target and BlackLight team.
A supernatural effect becomes visible to ordinary cameras.
The target deliberately forces the operation into a crowded space.
A high-profile person arrives without appearing on any schedule.
An evacuation places civilians directly across the extraction route.
Market, diplomatic, or transportation systems react visibly to the mission.
The client leaks a partial story to protect itself.
The operation remains locally secret but leaves evidence impossible to explain later.
hiddenAgendas: Charles believes this mission prevents a technology or event from arriving at the wrong point in history.
Eva wants proof of what the client concealed before BlackLight accepts further work from them.
The client wants leverage over a political rival rather than prevention of harm.
A supernatural sovereign wants BlackLight to establish precedent by acting inside contested territory.
The target expects intrusion and intends to feed BlackLight a controlled narrative.
The operation is also a test of whether a newly revealed Company member can be trusted with independent authority.
The real objective is identifying who responds when the visible target is threatened.
The client wants the asset delivered intact because it is one component in a larger concealed system.
Charles suspects the target contains a copy, continuation, or fragment of a person presumed dead.
The Watcher has prohibited one obvious solution, but Charles has not explained why.
The Company is correcting harm caused by an earlier mission whose survivors were never informed.
A rival team has been given a contradictory version of the same assignment.
complications: The person with legitimate access is frightened and may withdraw cooperation.
The target site is preparing for sale, transfer, or closure.
A routine repair places an unexpected civilian at the objective.
The client's maps are accurate but several years out of date.
A senior guard recognizes one operative from an earlier unrelated mission.
The mission asset is larger, more fragile, or more alive than the briefing implied.
The site's safety systems cannot distinguish sabotage from catastrophe.
The opposition has orders to preserve the asset even at the cost of abandoning the site.
A local community has its own plan and does not trust BlackLight.
The target's apparent leader is a decoy while staff quietly obey someone else.
The extraction route passes through a jurisdiction not included in the original agreement.
The team receives two mutually exclusive emergency requests at once.
A protected witness refuses to leave without another person.
The client attempts to change the objective after insertion.
The site contains evidence connecting the client to the target.
The requested asset can only be used by exposing the identity of the person who created it.
rewards: Defined Company compensation plus medical and legal support
A favor owed by a supernatural court or sovereign representative
Access to a captured archive relevant to a character's unresolved history
A protected safe site and resettlement support for affected civilians
A future requisition from BlackLight's specialized equipment inventory
Removal or repair of a false legal identity created by an earlier operation
Public evidence sufficient to stop the target through ordinary institutions
A contact inside the target organization
Custody of a harmless copy or research derivative
A formal apology and after-action disclosure from BlackLight leadership
Reduction of an existing debt, obligation, or supernatural claim
Information about who requested a previous unexplained mission
aftermath: The target survives and begins investigating BlackLight's support network.
The client receives the objective but disputes whether the team satisfied the hidden expectation.
A civilian witness asks BlackLight for protection rather than silence.
The operation becomes a jurisdictional complaint before a government, court, patron, or Watcher.
The asset proves authentic but creates a new containment responsibility.
The public explanation works locally while analysts elsewhere identify inconsistencies.
The site's workforce loses employment or housing and requires Company support.
A rival operative offers information in exchange for asylum.
The destroyed system transfers part of its function somewhere unknown.
The client becomes more dangerous because the mission succeeded.
The team preserves the truth but loses the paid objective.
A character's identity becomes connected to the operation despite successful extraction.
The target organization changes procedures, increasing difficulty for all future missions.
The recovered archive names an unexpected BlackLight ally.
The mission resolves the visible problem while revealing the larger campaign antagonist.
Charles admits that one critical briefing omission was his decision.
